title: EU Calls for De-escalation as Tigray Rebels Clash With Ethiopian Forces
detail: The European Union has called for de-escalation following reports of renewed armed clashes between Tigray rebels (TPLF) and Ethiopian federal forces in northern Ethiopia. The EU statement signals international concern over a potential resumption of large-scale conflict in the Tigray region, where a fragile ceasefire under the Pretoria Agreement has been under strain. Fighting in northern Ethiopia has drawn renewed diplomatic attention amid fears of a broader humanitarian crisis.

media.caption: EU calls for de-escalation as Tigray rebels clash with Ethiopian federal forces in renewed northern Ethiopia fighting

title: ENDF Claims 272 TPLF Fighters Killed in North Wollo Counteroffensive
detail: The Ethiopian National Defence Force said on Thursday, Sep 24, 2026 that it repelled coalition attacks across seven localities in Amhara's North Wollo zone (near Woldia and Kobo), claiming 272 Tigrayan fighters killed, 260 wounded, and several captured. 'Government forces launched a counter-offensive that inflicted heavy personnel and equipment losses on the TPLF,' the ENDF said in a statement. TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa responded that 'We are in the situation of full-blown war now.' No independent source has verified the ENDF's casualty figures.

media.caption: Ethiopia's army says it killed 272 Tigrayan fighters in a North Wollo counteroffensive

confidenceReason: The casualty figures rest solely on the ENDF's own statement; the TPLF has not confirmed or specifically disputed the numbers and no independent monitor has verified them.

title: Fighting Nears UNESCO Site Lalibela, Flights Suspended
detail: Ethiopian government forces deployed heavy weapons against Fano positions near the holy town of Lalibela in Amhara's North Wollo zone as fighting expanded from the Sep 23 offensive. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to and from Lalibela's airport on Sep 24, 2026, and the U.S. Embassy in Addis Ababa said it was aware of reports of active fighting near the UNESCO World Heritage site. Fighting was reported around the town rather than inside it.
